en.title: Maximum Number of Times the Target Word Can Be Taken With Rearrangement
en.description:
Each time, choose any characters from s that, after rearranging, form exactly the target t, then delete those characters; all other characters remain. Find the maximum number of target words that can be taken. The characters need not form a contiguous substring, and they need not spell t in their original order.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The two lines contain s and t. The original statement only specifies lowercase letters; on this site 1≤|s|,|t|≤200000 and the target is non-empty.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 0 and 2 respectively. In the third example each target uses two a's, so it can be taken only twice.
hints: Count the characters of s and t separately. The answer is the minimum, over every character that appears in t, of how many times it can be supplied, countS//countT.
